replies.author: Matic0B
replies.body:
Hello.

There is a WIP version of Clay Wars TE thats in the works already by me. 

I am also quite disappointed that I wasn't contacted by anyone (as the map creator of Clay Wars) about this earlier so I could tell you about the WIP TE version so I could have some input.

This map also ignores most of the things I thought about when making the original. Of course you couldn't know it since they were never publicly talked about but the biggest features were no wood and armor which limited teams quite a lot and made gameplay simpler. You adding diamonds, wood and even water completely throws away the simplistic feel I wanted to go for in the beginning. I don't want my map to be associated with something it never ment to be, thats why I test my maps before even posting them.

I don't have nothing against your map, just really disappointed I was not contacted.

replies.author: Matic0B
replies.body:
The MapDevs, specifically Legoche, the head MapDev, gave me permission. I had no way of contacting you. 

I won't blame you for not being able to contact me as I did remove contact methods from my profile. I don't know if /msg works with offline players like on OCN but that could be one way (if offline messaging works). Still don't think that the map developers (even if head mapdev) should be an excuse as its not their map.

If you wish I will change the name. I started with the Clay Wars map and ended with this.

You don't have to change anything because the map doesn't actually look that bad. The layout is very interesting and I think you did a good job at it. As long as you credit me as well, I won't complicate things.

A TE map has no realistic chance of working without key supplies such as Iron, Wood, and in a DTM case, Diamonds.

I'll have to disagree with this as maps can still work out in competitive play without some supplies such as Diamond and Iron. Wood is more of a needed resource but could also be replaced with stone if you put crafting tables already somewhere on the map. It limits defending to some extent but adds some possibilities such as buttons, slabs and pressure plates.

Already answered this above but I'll still say it here. Wood is very needed due to the defending posibilities but can also be replaced with stone. Still limits the gameplay but gives some possibilities as long as you place crafting tables on the map.

As for iron supplies, it can also work without those in some cases. Its an important thing on most maps and usually helps the maps competitive aspect but in some cases its not needed.

Even though Deepwind Jungle isn't DTM but is CTW on OCN, theres no Iron and the map works well for competitive. DTM is harder to create without things like Iron but its still possible

replies.body:
You do realize OCN had this policy too? That's why they could make gimmicky edits or remixes of maps on their too without permission because a lot of the people on that server had faded into obscurity. There's no problem with it, because I believe Oversoul and Eclipsen have had problems with their maps being edited and exactly what we do is follow what the author wants. Although I will agree with you that the way the current system for maps is a bit iffy (Who made this up?) the remixing of maps is actually a good feature meant for FUN. Not stealing maps.

He merely mentioned OCN because they appeared to use the same system as well and you were a regular OCN map maker and you seemed to have no problem with the way that they handled maps even though from what I see as Para mentioned, it appears to be the same?

Using the argument that "You aren't OCN" is sort of... annoying? I feel like it's a way for people to use as a cheap way to either prohibit Avicus development (You aren't doing this), throwing off the opposite argument because you're feeling emotional (This is sort of you, I can understand your feelings but this was unnecessary) and just plain being a dick (This isn't really you but you were being aggressive).

The system of remixes is more like a gimmick which isn't really meant to be taken seriously, it's more like a "If you got your hands on this map how much would you change?"

It's technically a joke map but it will be released to the public. The only credit that the remixer would get is for simply remixing it. The original author would still get most of the credit for making the original.

It's like a remixing music, no one has a problem with that so why should you have a problem with this? Do you want to introduce SOPA on maps? (Sorry but I'm also sort of a sarcastic person, I need to point out the hypocrisy so that you will see reason, not because I dislike you...)
